'''''Juncus conglomeratus''''', the '''compact rush''', is a perennial, herbaceous [[flowering plant]] [[species]] in the rush family [[Juncaceae]]. 

In the [[British Isles]] it is one of six [[rush species]] that can dominate lowland damp [[grassland]]s.<ref name=LGMH>[http://naturalengland.etraderstores.com/NaturalEnglandShop/Grassland The Lowland Grassland Management Handbook] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110317041420/http://naturalengland.etraderstores.com/NaturalEnglandShop/Grassland |date=2011-03-17 }} 2nd edition, A Crofts and R G Jefferson (eds) [[English Nature]] {{ISBN|1-85716-443-1}}, 1999</ref>{{citation needed|reason=poor source-not clear where to find the stated claim in this citation|date=June 2023}} In New Zealand, its habitats include lake margins, roadside drains and wet pastures. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Juncus conglomeratus |url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/juncus-conglomeratus/ |access-date=2025-07-05 |website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network |language=en}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
The species' geographical range includes the northwestern corners of Africa, almost all of Europe and the Caucasus region. It has been introduced and has become wild in Australia, New Zealand and North America.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Taxonomy Detail GRIN-Global |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxon/taxonomydetail?id=318195.%20Accessed%204%20July%202025. |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=npgsweb.ars-grin.gov}}</ref>

== Description ==
''Juncus conglomeratus'' forms large, dense tufts up to 1.2 m high with a dense bundle of roots.

Its '''stems''' are awl-shaped, stalked, vivid green, partially filled with a core (continuous, uninterrupted core), wrapped at the base (below ground level) with scaly brown leaf sheaths. The stems beneath the inflorescence are ribbed, while in the similar Scattered rush (''Juncus'' ''effusius'') they are smooth. 

The plant's '''leaves''' are exclusively abaxial, stalk-like.

The '''[[Inflorescence]]''' is a spherical head, about 1 cm long. Appears lateral because at the base a bract grows as an extension of the stem. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Juncus conglomeratus (bunch-flowered soft rush): Go Botany |url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/juncus/conglomeratus/ |access-date=2025-07-05 |website=gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org}}</ref>

The '''flower''' is small, 2-2.5 mm long, [[perianth]] - rust-colored, [[Stamen|stamens]] count ranges from 3-6. Blooms from June to August.

The '''fruit''' forms a capsule, with a small beak at the tip, length ranging from 1.5–3.2 mm.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juncus conglomeratus |url=https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/juncus-conglomeratus/ |access-date=2025-07-05 |website=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network |language=en}}</ref>

'''Seeds''' are small (up to 0.3 mm long), dark brown, egg-shaped oblong, laterally flattened, pointed at the end, dull. The weight of 1000 seeds is 0.01 g. [[File:Compact Rush (Juncus conglomeratus) - geograph.org.uk - 497518.jpg|none|thumb|Close-up of [[inflorescence]]|355x355px]]
== Variability ==
It has been observed to hybridize with ''Juncus effusus, Juncus inflexus'' and ''Juncus filiformis.''
